reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
Mondays used to be the worst day of the week. Not because of work, exactly, but because Monday was the receipt for whatever I'd done to myself Friday through Sunday. The headache. The vague dread. The scrolling back through texts to figure out what I'd said. By Monday afternoon I was already negotiating with Thursday.

Sober Mondays are a different animal. They're not thrilling. Nobody writes poems about a clear-headed Monday morning in late October, the light coming in a little slower, coffee that actually tastes like something, the small satisfaction of remembering last night. But this is where the life gets built. Not in the big dramatic moments — the first chip, the sunrise after a hard night, the trip you never thought you'd take sober. Those matter, but they're not the structure. The structure is Monday. The structure is showing up for the ordinary thing you said you'd do, when nobody's watching and nothing's on fire.

Aristotle had it right, or Durant did on his behalf: you don't become someone in a moment. You become them by repetition. Every unremarkable sober Monday is a brick. Stack enough of them and one day you look up and realize you've built something you actually want to live inside.
reflection.meditation: What's one small, ordinary thing I can show up for today — not because it's exciting, but because it's mine?

affirmations: I am building a life one ordinary day at a time, and today counts.
Today I get to be present for the small things I used to sleep through.
I am someone who keeps the quiet promises I make to myself.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a Monday that doesn't start in the hole. Grateful for coffee I can actually taste, a memory of yesterday that's mine to keep, and the strange luxury of a clear head on an ordinary morning. There was a version of me who couldn't have imagined this being enough — and here it is, more than enough.
gratitude.closing: One more day. That's the whole thing.
